newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaraguan armed gangs start to disarm.
newsitem.headline: Nicaraguan armed gangs start to disarm.

text.p: Two armed gangs with 23 members remaining from Nicaragua's civil war turned in their guns on Friday, the first progress in the government's peace talks with the gangs.

The gangs, loosely linked to the former Contra rebels, handed in their weapons to Nicaraguan Defence Minister Jaime Cuadra in exchange for promises of amnesty, land and credit at a ceremony 155 miles (250 km) east of Managua, a government press release said.
Each gang member also received a pair of jeans, a shirt, a pair of boots and two pairs of underwear, the government said.

"We no longer want to be at war. We want to leave these two and a half years of struggle behind and take up the plough to feed ourselves because we are sure President Arnoldo Aleman will fulfil his promises," gang leader Enrique Lumbi, alias "The Ant," said at the ceremony.
The second gang was led by Ricardo Ivan Perez, alias "Lester," the government said.
Aleman, who took office on Jan. 10, has set Feb. 28 as the deadline for 480 remaining gang members to lay down their arms or be treated as common criminals.
Nicaragua's civil war ended in 1990, but many former combatants later re-armed to protest what they said was the government's failure to fulfil the terms of the peace treaty.
The army estimated that 31 armed bands loosely linked to the Contras or left-wing Sandinista army operated in the north and central provinces of Jinotega, Matagalpa and Chontales.

Despite repeated government amnesties and help to reinsert into civilian life, the problem has not gone away. Since 1990, armed bands have killed 1,000 people, wounded 400 and kidnapped 600 civilians, according to army figures.
